artworks.title: Sleeping Hermaphroditus
artworks.artist: Unknown (Roman copy); mattress by Gian Lorenzo Bernini
artworks.description: The Borghese Hermaphrodite — the Carian fountain's afterlife in marble, languid until the other side reveals the biform body.

artworks.title: Hermaphroditus and the Nymph Salmacis
artworks.description: Spranger's Mannerist embrace — Salmacis clinging in the pool as Ovid's prayer fuses two bodies into one.

artworks.title: The Nymph Salmacis and Hermaphroditus
artworks.description: Navez's Neoclassical fountain — the Carian nymph and the youth at the water that will not let them part.

artworks.title: Sleeping Hermaphroditus (Palazzo Massimo)
artworks.artist: Roman copy after a Hellenistic original
artworks.year: 2nd century AD (copy); Greek original 2nd century BC
artworks.description: The Palazzo Massimo sleeper — another Roman cast of the Hellenistic type that made Salmacis' myth marble.

popCulture.title: Sleeping Hermaphroditus
popCulture.description: The Borghese Hermaphrodite — Hellenistic languor with Bernini's mattress — remains the myth's most famous body: Salmacis' embrace made marble.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book IV tells the Carian fountain — the nymph who will not let go, the prayer that softens every man who bathes, and the biform body that names the figure.

popCulture.title: Hermaphroditus
popCulture.description: Child of Hermes and Aphrodite — the Salmacis episode still supplies the West's vocabulary for dual-sexed form.
